name: BARBELL BENCH PRESS
description: A compound press that builds chest thickness, triceps, and pressing power from a stable bench.
instructions: Lie flat on the bench with feet planted firmly on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and unrack it over your chest.
Lower the bar under control until it lightly touches your mid-chest.
Drive the bar back up to full lock-out, keeping your shoulder blades pinned.

name: INCLINE DUMBBELL PRESS
description: Targets the upper chest and front delts by pressing from an inclined bench angle.
instructions: Set the bench to a 30-45 degree incline and sit with a dumbbell in each hand.
Press the dumbbells up until your arms are fully extended above your chest.
Lower them slowly until your upper arms are just below parallel.
Press back up, squeezing your chest at the top of the movement.

name: CONVENTIONAL DEADLIFT
description: A full-body pull that builds raw strength through the posterior chain, back, and grip.
instructions: Stand with the bar over mid-foot and grip it just outside your knees.
Set your back flat, chest up, and hips down before initiating the pull.
Drive through the floor, keeping the bar close to your shins and thighs.
Lock out tall at the top, then lower the bar back down with control.

name: LAT PULLDOWN
description: Builds a wider back and stronger pulling strength using a controlled cable movement.
instructions: Sit at the machine and grip the bar wider than shoulder-width.
Brace your core and pull the bar down to your upper chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom of the pull.
Slowly return the bar up until your arms are fully extended.

name: BARBELL BACK SQUAT
description: The king of lower-body lifts, building quads, glutes, and total-body bracing strength.
instructions: Set the bar across your upper back and step out of the rack.
Brace your core and sit back and down until hips drop below your knees.
Keep your chest up and knees tracking over your toes throughout.
Drive through your heels to stand back up to full extension.

name: WALKING LUNGE
description: A unilateral leg builder that improves balance, quad and glute strength with every step.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand and stand tall with feet together.
Step forward into a lunge, lowering your back knee toward the floor.
Push off your front foot to bring your back leg through into the next step.
Continue alternating legs for the full distance or rep count.

name: STANDING BARBELL CURL
description: A classic bicep builder that isolates the arms with strict, controlled curls.
instructions: Stand tall holding the bar with an underhand, shoulder-width grip.
Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides, curl the bar up toward your chest.
Squeeze your biceps hard at the top of the movement.
Lower the bar back down slowly under full control.

name: TRICEPS ROPE PUSHDOWN
description: Isolates the triceps with constant cable tension for a strong lockout and definition.
instructions: Attach a rope to the high pulley and grip both ends with elbows tucked in.
Push the rope down until your arms are fully extended, splitting the rope at the bottom.
Squeeze your triceps hard at full extension.
Slowly let the rope rise back up without flaring your elbows.

name: OVERHEAD SHOULDER PRESS
description: Builds strong, capped shoulders and pressing stability from a standing or seated position.
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height, palms facing forward.
Brace your core and press the dumbbells straight overhead.
Lock out fully without flaring your ribs or arching your back.
Lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height with control.

name: LATERAL RAISE
description: Isolates the side delts to build width and a rounder, more capped shoulder shape.
instructions: Stand tall holding a light dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise your arms out to the sides.
Lift until your arms are roughly parallel with the floor.
Lower back down slowly and repeat without swinging.

name: RUSSIAN TWIST
description: A rotational core movement that builds obliques and total midsection stability.
instructions: Sit on the floor with knees bent and lean back to a 45-degree angle.
Hold a medicine ball with both hands in front of your chest.
Rotate your torso to tap the ball on the floor beside your hip.
Rotate to the opposite side and repeat, keeping your core braced.

name: PLANK
description: A foundational isometric hold that builds core stability and total-body tension.
instructions: Set up on your forearms and toes, elbows stacked under your shoulders.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes to keep your hips level.
Keep a straight line from head to heels without sagging or piking.
Hold the position for the full duration, breathing steadily throughout.
